text: The RLS objective weights past errors by a forgetting factor (mu in the text, lambda_f in the lab). What does choosing a value below 1 do?
choices: It weights all samples equally, recovering ordinary least squares
It forces the reservoir weights to slowly drift over time
It down-weights recent samples to stabilize the estimate
It weights recent samples more than older ones, enabling tracking of non-stationary statistics
explanation: The factor mu^(t-s) exponentially discounts older data, so mu < 1 emphasizes recent samples and lets the readout track drifting/non-stationary statistics. mu = 1 gives equal weighting (ordinary LS); it never touches the reservoir weights; and it up-weights recent, not older, data.
